question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for collagen remodeling and pelvic ligament laxity during pregnancy?
explanation: Relaxin specifically targets the collagen matrix of pelvic ligaments to soften and increase flexibility for childbirth. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h1)

question: Why is generalized joint laxity considered a physiological paradox during pregnancy?

options.A: It prevents weight gain while accelerating joint degeneration
options.B: It decreases pelvic mobility while increasing flexibility in the wrists
options.C: It facilitates birth yet increases susceptibility to musculoskeletal injury
options.D: It builds bone density while simultaneously causing muscle wasting

explanation: The softening of ligaments is essential for fetal passage through the pelvis, but it leaves joints vulnerable to strain and misalignment. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h1)

question: In which direction does the maternal center of gravity shift during pregnancy?
explanation: The expanding uterus and growing fetus alter body mass distribution, pulling the center of gravity forward and upward. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h2)

question: What is the primary postural adaptation a pregnant woman makes to compensate for her shifted center of gravity?

options.A: Shifting weight exclusively onto the upper extremities
options.B: Flexing the cervical spine and rounding the shoulders forward
options.C: Locking the knees and widening the base of gait
options.D: Hyperextending the upper torso and tilting the pelvis anteriorly

explanation: To keep from falling forward, the body leans backward, causing lumbar lordosis and anterior pelvic tilt. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h2)

question: What term describes the exaggerated inward curvature of the lower back experienced during pregnancy?
explanation: Lordosis is the normal inward curvature of the lumbar spine, which becomes significantly exaggerated during pregnancy. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h3)

question: Why does stretching of the abdominal wall during pregnancy contribute directly to back pain?

options.A: It directly compresses the spinal nerves within the spinal canal
options.B: It forces the pelvis to rotate posteriorly and lock the hip joints
options.C: It impairs the core stabilizing muscles, forcing the back muscles to work harder
options.D: It pulls the vertebrae apart and causes excessive fluid loss in discs

explanation: Weakened or stretched abdominal muscles fail to support the spine, leaving back extensors to bear the full weight of posture. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h3)

question: Which anatomical structure connects the two innominate bones at the anterior midline of the pelvis?
explanation: The symphysis pubis is the fibrocartilaginous joint situated between the left and right pubic bones. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h4)

question: A pregnant patient complains of sharp pubic pain and difficulty stepping into her wrapper or trousers. Which condition is she most likely experiencing?
explanation: Movections requiring single-leg weight-bearing or asymmetric hip abduction exacerbate symphysis pubis dysfunction. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h4)

question: Which nerve is compressed within the wrist to cause gestational carpal tunnel syndrome?
explanation: Fluid retention and edema narrow the carpal tunnel, compressing the median nerve and causing paresthesia in the hand. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h5)

question: What is the primary cause of dependent lower extremity edema in the third trimester of pregnancy?

options.A: Excessive dietary sodium intake combined with heavy exercise
options.B: Rapid breakdown of red blood cells in the lower leg veins
options.C: Complete failure of the right side of the maternal heart
options.D: Increased venous pressure from uterine compression on pelvic vessels

explanation: The heavy uterus impedes venous return from the lower limbs, raising hydrostatic pressure and driving fluid into interstitial tissues. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h5)

question: During the second stage of labour, what movement does the sacrum typically undergo to enlarge the pelvic outlet?
explanation: The sacrum moves backward during crowning, increasing the anteroposterior diameter of the pelvic outlet for the baby. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h6)

question: Why is careful positioning of a labouring woman under epidural anesthesia essential for her musculoskeletal health?

options.A: She cannot feel normal pain signals that warn of excessive joint strain or awkward positioning
options.B: Epidural medications dissolve bone calcium and weaken the femur shaft
options.C: Nerve blocks cause immediate paralysis of the upper back muscles
options.D: Anesthesia permanently tightens the pelvic ligaments and prevents dilation

explanation: When pain perception is blunted by regional anesthesia, patients cannot self-adjust away from harmful joint hyperextension or twisting. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h6)

question: What is the term for the separation of the rectus abdominis muscles that frequently persists into the postpartum period?
explanation: Diastasis recti refers to the parting of the rectus abdominis muscle bellies along the midline connective tissue during pregnancy. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h7)

question: Why are postpartum women still at risk for joint injuries several weeks after giving birth?

options.A: Breastfeeding causes immediate mineralization and softening of all skeletal joints
options.B: Newborn care requires movements that only men can perform safely
options.C: Relaxin remains active in the circulation and joint tissues for a considerable time postpartum
options.D: The sudden weight loss in the abdomen destabilizes the spinal column permanently

explanation: Even after birth, residual relaxin keeps ligaments lax until complete endocrine and tissue recovery occurs. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h7)

question: Which nursing intervention is most appropriate for a pregnant client experiencing symphysis pubis dysfunction?

options.A: Encouraging high-impact aerobic exercise to strengthen ligaments
options.B: Applying a pelvic support belt and advising small, equal steps
options.C: Massaging the pubic symphysis with deep tissue pressure daily
options.D: Recommending strict bed rest in the prone position for weeks

explanation: Pelvic belts stabilize the ring externally, and avoiding wide strides reduces shear stress on the pubic symphysis. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h8)

question: What is the primary rationale for teaching pregnant women the log-rolling technique when getting out of bed?

options.A: It prevents the development of gestational carpal tunnel syndrome
options.B: It reduces dependent ankle edema by accelerating lower limb blood flow
options.C: It minimizes strain on the stretched abdominal wall and vulnerable lumbar spine
options.D: It encourages normal fetal movement and prevents breech positioning

explanation: Log-rolling keeps the spine aligned and avoids twisting the weak abdominal wall and overloaded lumbar vertebrae. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h8)
